newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Compaq ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Compaq ahead of earnings.

text.p: A quick recoil in a technology sector rally today prompted a wave of exodus in option positions on Compaq Computer Corp before the firm's earnings results due out Wednesday, traders said.
"Compaq (stock) hasn't backed off as much as some of the other ones, but I've got guys who are locking in (profits) today," said Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategy at EVEREN Securities.
"They had a nice ride and they've seen what happened to Intel, so they're just getting out today," he added.
Compaq shares, which have been on a healthy uptrend since dipping to a minor bottom at 50-7/8 in early September, were trading at 74-3/8 in late trade, up 2-1/2 on the day.

October 70 call on the Pacific Stock Exchange (PSE) saw volume of 3,051 lots by late trade, relatively heavy for such an in-the-money Compaq option. Traders said the open interest in the contract was most likely to have fallen today.
Compaq November 75.0 and October 75.0 calls were among the most actively traded contracts on PSE, with turnover of 4,606 and 3,825 lots respectively.
Most technology stocks opened sharply higher after news late on Monday of a 40-percent jump in Intel Corp's third quarter profit, but ran out of steam by mid-morning.
Intel's per-share earnings came in at $1.48 against a consensus estimate of $1.25.
Intel shares, which briefly shot up to a fresh all-time high of 114-1/4 early in the session, stood at 111-1/8, up 3-1/2 on the day.
Chicago Board Options Exchange technology index and Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index were back down to around Monday closes after an early spike up.
Implied volatility for the November 75.0 call was at about 44 percent, slightly above its normal level of about 37, said Harrison Roth, first vice president of Cowen & Co.
He said while Compaq could extend its rally on a strong earnings report like Intel did, but agreed that even Intel soon came under pressure from profit-taking.
"On the other hand, disappointment would be easy," Roth added.
According to First Call, analysts' estimates for Compaq's quarterly earnings averaged $1.07 per share versus 0.89 a year earlier.

Intel options were by far the most heavily traded contracts today, with November 115 and October 110 calls trading more than 10,000 lots on the American Stock Exchange, as the stock gyrated in a wide range.

Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co, noted that the technology sector, which has led the market's recent rally, appeared to be the main source of volatility for the entire stock market.
"Technology continues to provide the greatest amount of option volume and volatility," he said.
